utterances.text: Mr. Hannis showed you, on the second page of this document, paragraph 9, where it says that you, as assistant minister, pursuant to this order, are also a member of the staff. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, it is true, isn't it, that you never even received an order from some alleged staff of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of your colleagues, including under-secretaries of the ministry and other individuals, received any sort of an order that would have the heading of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of anybody receiving such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said heading of the staff of the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that you never attended or heard of a meeting of the staff of the Ministry of Interior being held?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I neither heard of a meeting ever being held, nor did I attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, given that you were assistant minister and a member of the staff, it would be logical to expect that, had a document of such a staff ever been issued, you would have seen it; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, sir, the Law on All People's Defence and Social Self-Protection, and the Law on The Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska, or, rather, the federal Law on All People's Defence and Social Self-Protection, that federal law was simply taken over by the Assembly of Republika Srpska. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Like the majority of laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact that the Law on Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska had very few differences as compared to the law of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were very similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you will agree with me, won't you, that the MUP of Republika Srpska was duty-bound to also adopt a so-called wartime plan; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: However, due to events and the speed with which they were taking place, such a plan was not adopted in the course of 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't adopted, but there probably are additional reasons for that. And if I may expand on that. We lived in one state where all plans were alike. And I have to be creative in phrasing this. The plans were drafted with scenarios where there were attacks from the west and from the east, and one needed great minds to create such plans from scratch. And that was an additional reason. That was also the problem we were encountering; we had neither resources nor people capable of drafting such plans, let alone the conditions that were difficult at the time. This was just by way of clarification. So the concept was completely different. The whole system was created on different foundations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, we're about to move to your meetings with Mico Stanisic in 1992. I would just like to explore some general views and positions right now. It's true, isn't it, that Mr. Mico Stanisic, as minister, insisted that the police do the tasks that were under its jurisdiction under the law, to take care of law and order rather than take part in combat and wartime operations. That's true, and that was the position of the minister; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Also, you, as assistant minister in charge of suppressing crime, received a carte blanche from Mico Stanisic, the minister, to do your work; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And when I say a "carte blanche," I meant that you were to take action in accordance with powers that you had under the law; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And to that effect, I think that you gave an example whereby at one point in time the minister gave powers to you and Mr. Karisik, commander of the special police detachment, to use members of that special unit when you saw fit, when there was a need for that; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Planojevic, the role of the ministry and the ministry administrations is first and foremost of an instructive nature; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They instruct and coordinate. That is their role.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very briefly, give us explanations for the instructive role of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instructive role means that the general policy that guides the work of the administration is set, is given guide-lines, instructive enactments or instructions, and possibly, in very complex cases, inspectors are to get involved in operative work. But, again, only to give instructions, not to actually carry out work or implement it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And to that effect, you, as chief of the administration for crime suppression, sent out inspectors from your administration precisely in order to give instructions to some CSBs and SJBs in 1992, to those that you were able to reach physically; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that you also had cases where some inspectors that you had sent out on a mission never came back to the ministry but, rather, they would flee abroad. They would move out abroad while being on official mission; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that is quite telling of the situation as it was in 1992. It is a good illustration of what the discipline of the members of the ministry was.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It speaks of the entire society, what the society was like, not of how disciplined persons were. We had problems in providing livelihood and safety for our families, and I personally didn't have such great problems but others did. So it is not up to me to judge them, to condemn them. That's how the times were. You can't even imagine it now. And I hope for you that you -- you personally would never experience this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely why I'm asking you this, because the context is very important for the case. The context of the entire situation. I think that you said that this also involved the personal courage of various individuals. Not everybody was equally brave. And that didn't get recorded in the transcript. Can you please confirm that you said that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I didn't understand that this was a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Now to go back to what you discussed with Mr. Hannis on Friday, that is to say, meetings with Mico Stanisic in 1992. If I remember -- if I understood you well, you mentioned a total of five encounters, and I will enumerate them for you now. The first one was in early May at the school in Vraca; the second one you mentioned was in early June at the Kosuta hotel; the third meeting was in late June, accidental chance meeting in front of the Bistrica hotel; the fourth meeting was around the 20th of July, when you argued with the minister and resigned; and the fifth meeting was sometime in October of 1992, when, again, you met by chance in the forest when the -- the defence lines at Praca fell. Did I summarise all your meetings with the minister in 1992 correctly?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you met him for the first time in early May in Vraca, you met Mico Stanisic in the presence of Mr. Mico -- Cedo Kljajic, under-secretary for public security; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And, among other things, you discussed how, according to you and to Cedo Kljajic, Mr. Momo Mandic should not be deputy minister of the interior; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That was so because you had some indications and also because of the fact that he was having contacts with Skrbo and Vuletic, persons who were - let me put it like this - people who were on the shady side?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the indicia that you had -- or, rather, except for the indicia that you had, you did not have any evidence that would make it possible for you to have Mr. Mandic and the other persons taken through some kind of legitimate criminal proceedings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You made a proposal to the minister; you presented him with your position on the issue. However, even then it was clear to you that Mico Stanisic does not have the authority to replace Momo Mandic from this position of deputy minister. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did already tell the OTP that the procedure was the same for appointing both the minister and the deputy minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the procedure is the same for appointing both the minister and the deputy minister," by that you mean that this appointment is something that is reached, that it's a decision reached by high-level organs and more important people who are in charge of making such decisions?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the law prescribes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your next meeting was held in early June in the Kosuta hotel.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Upon my request.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, you asked the minister -- or, rather, you presented to the minister that the withdrawal of the special detachment from Vraca would create certain problems. Let's now -- let's not get into that because you've already testified about it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, if I understood you correctly, you also told him about what you knew about certain Vlahovic, Batko; you told the minister about him?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was on that occasion or maybe when we just meant accidentally, later on. The way I remember it, it was when we meant in front of the Bistrica hotel. Because during the first meeting I didn't have the information that I told him about at this later meeting. One must bear in mind that it was all happening within a short period of time and I cannot be precise about the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand you completely. It's been a long time ago, and I do not insist on specific dates here. I would just like to put things into a proper context. As I understood you, during your stay in Belgrade, you had heard from a friend of yours, so that was in Belgrade, when you heard about Batko who also used to go to Belgrade, that he was bragging in Belgrade about crimes he had committed in Sarajevo. That's where you got your information.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But I must add something, because things come to my mind as I speak. Upon my return, I went to a Croatian family's flat at Grbavica. I was aware that people who were non-Serbs know more, or at least talk more, about it. I think the surname of this family was Mihic. They told me that they had heard this Batica being mentioned. So that was -- motivated me to take further steps, and I explained the steps I took.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After your return, in addition to going to speak to the Croats that you knew at Grbavica, you also asked one of your colleagues, an inspector, to check the information you had, and he did tell you that there were certain indicia, or at least rumours, that this Batko was involved in some kind of crime.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You informed the minister about it; the minister told you that he will inform the Main Staff of the VRS; and he also tasked you with monitoring the situation, namely, whether the army is going to take measures in relation to this Batko character. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You did as you were told, and after a certain period of time, he was arrested by the military police and detained in the military prison at Lukavica, which is within Sarajevo; am I right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But before that, he had been informed by someone that the police had started -- had started taking measures, and he was not in the area for, as I was told, about 20 days. Upon his return, he was arrested. I know that for a fact because it -- it was immediately known that this person was arrested by the military police and that he's at Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: When you reach a convenient point, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just one question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Later on, you received information that he was released by the military authorities from that prison, but you don't know anything else about it?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This arrest of his may have taken place at the time when I resigned and I wasn't there. He was absent for a period of 20 days, and it may be that I resigned in the meantime, and all the information I have was second-hand information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this would be a good moment, Your Honours, because I would like to move to the next meeting, and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We return in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Planojevic, we've reached the third meeting now, your third meeting with Mr. Mico Stanisic. You said you accidentally ran into him in front of the Bistrica hotel. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On Friday, a few questions were put to you about this meeting. You remembered it. Mr. Stanisic had a German Shepherd with him, which was unusual, and my learned friend asked you about it, and then you made some jokes about this German Shepherd dog. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you were joking on that occasion, you said it was a German Shepherd that was owned by Josip Broz, Tito, during the Second World War and it was called Rex the dog.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Planojevic, for a long period of time there were jokes circulated about Mr. Stanisic concerning the fact that in 1973 he was honoured, as a member of a youth organisation, to take the -- to take the staff on occasion of Tito's birthday. He was the one who carried it from Sarajevo. I don't know what the proper word for this relay staff that people pass on in English, but it was one of the traditions of former Yugoslavia. On the 24th of May, which was the National Youth Day, President Tito would be handed this baton by a representative of the youth organisation of former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact also that this was a honour awarded only to the best among the youth.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is also a fact that the concept of brotherhood and unity was one of the central elements, pillars, of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia; am I right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your answer hasn't made the transcript -- oh, it has. I apologise. So, on the basis of what we've just said, one can conclude that Mr. Mico Stanisic neither at that time nor later had any dislike for people of different ethnic groups of former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's absolutely true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that was also the case in 1992, when you became assistant minister. And you know Mr. Stanisic since 1973, or even before, from your school days.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know each other since 1971, and he never in any action or statement of his would show that he had that kind of attitude.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any such elements pronounced in him, he wouldn't have been honoured to carry this baton for President Tito. You already told my learned colleagues what the topic of the discussions were on that occasion, so I won't go into that. And then your next meeting took place on or about 19 or 20 July, after your return from Belgrade, when you had an argument with Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understood your testimony on Friday correctly, you had information that he was looking for you. You found him sitting in an office or a room in a hotel together with Momo Mandic. They were just having a conversation of informal nature?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleagues from the administration, or the employees, told me that he'd been looking for me for the two or three days preceding that and that I should report to him immediately. But I arrived in the evening hours, so I went to see him in the morning next day. And upon my arrival at the Bistrica hotel, I asked where he was. I think he even had a room there; it was apartment 305, I think. But he wasn't there, and the people at the desk told me that he was in one of the rooms, and that's how I found him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your next meeting was sometime in October 1992, when you met him somewhere in a forest after the lines at Praca fell, when Mico Stanisic was there to visit his parents. That was in October 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It may have been September, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think you told my learned colleague - and I'm not sure whether it was today, early today, or on Friday - you told him that you remember that, on that occasion, when you had met Mico Stanisic in the forest, that with him were his driver, Jasarevic, and an escort of his, Goran Abazovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Planojevic, in addition to the meetings with the minister that we discussed, during the direct examination you also mentioned two meetings with Branko Djeric, who was the prime minister. Do you remember talking about that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The meetings with prime minister, Mr. Djeric, they were not official meetings, were they?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One was arranged, when I brought some written material. But the first one, the first one was informal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the first occasion, you went to see him together with a professor.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vaso Dragovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you went to have a cup of coffee with Professor Vaso Dragovic, and then Professor Dragovic invited Prime Minister Djeric to join you. And you'd known Prime Minister Djeric because you are from the same town and you know each other from way back.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your second meeting was, as you told us, four or five days after the meeting you had had with Minister Stanisic at Kosuta hotel. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, please, on that second occasion, you also discussed this Batko. Batko Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since you had a conversation with the minister four or five days prior to that, when the minister told you that he would inform or, rather, discuss with the men from the Main Staff about the problem, you had no reason to doubt that Mr. Stanisic would actually talk to the army representatives about the arrest of this Batko Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can elaborate, but, please, go on with your questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So that your conversation with Prime Minister Djeric does not mean that you requested him to intervene because you fostered doubts that Minister Stanisic would intervene with the military bodies.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't suspect that. But the situation being what it was, and it was serious, the prime minister asked me, once I had spoken about the problems I had had earlier, I added that I had spoken with the minister. And I considered that to be a serious problem. And I said to him, Let's not delay tackling this problem. Some people, as you know, don't like to communicate without authority. I don't want to say more because given my experience with the press, I really must watch my Ps and Qs. But the prime minister was a man of authority, and I don't know who had spoken to him, whether it was the president or the General Staff. The prime minister would have said if he had been against that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand correctly, you mentioned the case of Batko Vlahovic to Prime Minister Djeric. Firstly, because you considered that a serious problem; and, secondly, because you thought that the prime minister doubtlessly had -- would be respected more in military circles than the minister.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The army and the police weren't really on friendly terms, even in peacetime. There was always a sort of rivalry, who was more important.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The prime minister then spoke to somebody; you or I don't know who. And, at any rate, after some time, Batko Vlahovic was, indeed, arrested. We have made that clear, haven't we?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were on friendly terms with Mr. Djeric, right, because you knew him before he became prime minister, because you hailed from the same place?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We are, even now, on good terms. We have always been.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: During those two encounters with Mr. Djeric in May and June 1992, did the prime minister complain to you about Minister Stanisic in any way?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't explain about the minister, but there was a problem with Momo. And at one point in time, maybe later, he told me that it was about -- that it was time for change.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "Momo," you mean Momo Mandic, who was minister of justice at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric didn't confide in you or inform you that he had a problem with the minister who allegedly didn't inform him, so he wasn't aware of the security situation in the territory of the RS. Did he mention any of that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't. I didn't spend so much time with the prime minister. We only discussed two or three matters. It lasted half an hour only.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were assistant minister of the police. And since you were - and even now - are friends with Mr. Djeric, certainly if he had had a problem with the police, he would have told you. Or do you have a reason to doubt that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose he would have told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me show you document 1D98, which is an order by Mr. Djeric dated 25 May 1992 sent to the MUP, to the attention of the under-secretary for public security, Mr. Cedo Kljajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [Interpretation] 1D98.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Still not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It's document 1D98. And it is marked 1D00-0496. The English document is the right one, but we also need the Serbian version. Could we please enlarge it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document is dated 25 May 1992. I think it was signed by Mr. Trbojevic, who was vice or deputy prime minister; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would seem so, judging by what's written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was signed by Mr. Trbojevic, by -- who was deputy prime minister, on behalf of the prime minister, Mr. Djeric. And here, the Ministry of the Interior is sent the decision of the cabinet, dated 25 May, obliging them to collect information and submit a report about the safety of people and property. And in the conclusion it says: With special regard to facts concerning vehicles from TAS Sarajevo, a car factory in Vogosca, all in Ilidza, et cetera. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These are also matters that you discussed in your conversation with Mr. Djeric; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show 1D62 to the witness. The 65 ter number is 138.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you are familiar with this document, sir. It's dated 26 May, which is the following day after the document we have just seen, where government demands information from the ministry urgently. And this document is dated 26 May, which is the following day. And it says: "Since it is essential that we should urgently write a report for the Government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, you are required to provide information about offences against people and property in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." And then what follows are instructions as to how this should be done. And on page 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please turn the page. Could we please see page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You see here, halfway through the page under the heading Roman V, describe especially serious offences. The SJB of Vogosca is especially tasked to do that with regard to car theft; and the SJB of Ilidza with regard to oil theft.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It says the deadline to submit the report is 31 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see page 4 of the English translation. Let's stick to the page we see in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you see that this was signed on behalf of Mico Stanisic. I believe it says: "For the minister." And do you happen to know whose signature this is?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Cedo Kljajic?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So on the day after the request made by the cabinet, we see that the ministry required the CSBs to submit relevant information to -- to act upon the request of the government; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Among others, your administration, and you as its chief, sent two inspectors, Mr. Drago Borovcanin and Milomir Orasanin, to carry out an audit of the SJBs of Vogosca and Ilijas round about the 27th and 28th of May. I suppose that it had to do with the request of the cabinet and the instruction of the minister.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, somebody informed me. I arrived from Belgrade on the 27th, and this was already prepared. I basically just approved it. It wasn't a real audit, because that wasn't possible under the circumstances. We just went there to see what things were like and make an assessment what was in place and what wasn't. The crime department consisted of one man whose name was Stanko in Vogosca, and that was all there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'll show you P989, which is 65 ter 397. Tab 89. This is a report which was shown to you by Mr. Hannis. On the title page, it reads: "Report on the work of the Vogosca and Ilijas SJBs." It's dated 30 May.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's see page 2, please. I called P989, which is 65 ter 397, page 2. Could we see it, please. The English translation too. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It says here: On the 27th and 28th of May, 1992, the Ministry Inspectors Drago Borovcanin and Milomir Orasanin visited the Vogosca and Ilijas SJBs and reviewed their work on that occasion. It's very true, as you said, they went to see how these two SJBs worked, Vogosca and Ilijas; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I have a correction. They were sent by Cedo. Mico called me on the phone the following day. He asked about some instructions, what he should do. So Cedo Kljajic had sent them before I came back from --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Cedo Kljajic was the under-secretary?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Under-secretary for public security, and he was authorised to send out your inspectors; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the only one who could do so for the police and the crime service. He was the only one apart from the minister who could do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to comment on the last paragraph. And I follow up upon what you said, that in Vogosca they only had one man in crime enforcement. And here it says -- or, rather, here we can see these proposals made by your inspectors, that -- namely, that Zivko Lazarevic. And he's the one person who worked on -- in crime enforcement in Vogosca; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And it says here that the proposal was for Lazarevic, Zivko, given his experience and knowledge of the area, be appointed chief; whereas Branislav Vlaco, hereto inspector in the form Sarajevo CSB, be appointed to duties and tasks of inspector for crime prevention. Which means that he was to be inspector for crime prevention in the administration for crime prevention at the Vogosca SJB; right? That was the proposal?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We will get back to Branislav Vlaco, but I first want to show you the following document. But just to conclude. On the 25th of May, we saw the first document from the government, whereby the government issued instruction to the ministry to provide urgently some information. On the 26th of May, the ministry issued order to CSBs to provide such information. And, at the same time, the ministry sent out, on the 27th and 28th of May, some people to review the work of some SJBs. And all of this happened within these three or four days; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see based on the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this report was sent out on the 30th of May; whereas, we saw that the final deadline for sending out the report, based on the decision of the ministry, was the 31st of May; right? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will show you 1D106 now, which is 65 ter 1398. This is a report dated the 12th of July, 1992. This report was prepared by the operative workers of the Romanija-Birac CSB who sent this report to their chief, Zoran Cvijetic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They sent it to their chief and to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To the ministry, not the minister.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You're quite right. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We will see subsequently it says, On the 3rd of July, 1992, operatives of the Sarajevo CSB were sent by the chief of that CSB to the Vogosca SJB and that they were tasked with reviewing the crime situation in the territory of that municipality. And further on, on page 1, it says: "It was concluded that the crime service in Vogosca SJB did not exist, and special concern was expressed over cases of stealing new cars from the TAS Sarajevo car factory grounds from which 2300 cars had been stolen." This was discussed on Friday, this theft of cars from TAS. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And to put everything in context, your evidence was that you, on the 2nd of June, went to a meeting in Vogosca, Ilidza, and Ilijas, and that on that occasion you talked to the commander of the military unit which secured the TAS car factory in Vogosca; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It wasn't me. It's -- it was that his commander, the brigade commander, communicated with him in my presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But if I understood you well, you talked to the commander of the brigade and that during the conversation, and as you urged him to improve the security of the factory, the commander of the unit came to him, telling him that precisely on that day somebody had removed, without authorisation, 20 vehicles and that he was unable to do anything about it.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. He went back to Skipina. And this was while the meeting was under way between the people I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. And I mention it because it's quite an unusual incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just a comment. It is clear that on the 27th and 28th of May your people went there. You went there on the 2nd of June. But despite the proposals and suggestions and review of the situation, it is obvious that in early July the situation was not significantly different at the Vogosca SJB; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This report will tell us why that was the case. On this page, we'll see that these two operatives of the CSB explain what kind of problems they encountered upon arriving there: namely, that the chief had gone to Serbia; that they were unable to go into the office because, allegedly, the escort of the chief who had the keys to the office had also gone to Serbia; and to put it short, their work at the Vogosca SJB was obstructed. This is what we can derive from this report; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I have the right document on my screen. Page 2; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite follow, but that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It says here that on the following day, upon arriving at the Vogosca SJB, we learned that the chief had gone to Serbia and would come back in two or three days. And then it says: Following this, we talked to the commander of the station, asking him to unlock two offices of the crime department, to which he said that the keys were with a certain Radenko who had gone to Serbia together with the chief.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The penultimate sentence reads that it was agreed that a crime service was to be established comprising Vlaco, Brano, as head of the service, hereto worker of the service and CSB Sarajevo. And this is the same Brano Vlaco who, in the previous document, was proposed by your inspectors; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we see the last page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Based on this, we can see what were the reasons for such a situation at Vogosca. Finally, on the 9th of July, they managed to have a meeting with the chief, and they say that they expressed grave criticism concerning the centre and the work of municipal authorities. And then in the last two sentences they say, in addition to this, at the meeting, the opinion was expressed that the personnel policy at the Vogosca SJB can be formulated only by the chief of the SJB and his staff and that nobody from MUP and the municipality could appoint people in his institution. And then it was said at the meeting that they, the workers who came to inspect, were non- -- not wanted and not needed and that they should have come before. It is hard to comprehend this attitude, isn't it? But it is also good illustration of the situation as it was at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were very many such examples. What is curious is that wherever there were combat activities going on, the situation was always like this. First of all, they did not have enough staff; and, in addition to that, they also had people with weapons imposing their will.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And following all that, due to these combat activities and the situation that a particular municipality encountered, you objectively were unable to do anything about it.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. And this is why in one of the documents they stated that all traces need to be documented regardless of what happened and where it happened so that people could be prosecuted eventually. Because we were quite aware that in such radical situations it was impossible to do anything until everything was properly documented, let alone in combat situations. So this is why they said in that document that they should make every effort to record and document evidence and that when the conditions were ripe, something would be done about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We will get to that document too. But, here, we can see that the chief of the SJB directly said to the inspectors from the superior CSB that they were unwanted there, underlying that personnel policy within the Vogosca SJB would not be directed either by the superior CSB or the MUP. When I asked you whether this was one of the typical features of the condition, you said yes. Is it because you had in mind examples of such arbitrary behaviour by certain chiefs of SJBs?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And given -- or, rather, if there were combat operations in a particular municipality, then, naturally, there were many armed individuals there, belonging either to the TO, or paramilitaries, or the Army of Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. People were trying to defend the positions, to maintain the lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you will agree with me, Mr. Planojevic, won't you, if -- or when -- if you wanted to use your powers, you from the MUP, you could have come into a situation where you would be criticised for undermining the combat powers of the military in a certain territory; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Especially in that area down there. You did not dare do anything because people didn't have enough men for combat and they were happy to get anybody they could, and commanders used anybody they could. And this is why things happened that should not have been allowed to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now that we have touched upon Brano Vlaco, when asked by my learned friend Mr. Hannis, you explained how they -- there were two individuals with the same first and last name. Do you remember that? One of them was inspector for corporate crime at the town SUP of Sarajevo before the war; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I remember your comment well, this was a man with a moustache; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's true to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That Brano Vlaco went to Vogosca, and that is precisely this Brano Vlaco mentioned in these two documents as a man nominated to work in the department for crime suppression in Vogosca; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They nominated him because he lived in Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What is important with -- for me, however, is that the two documents that we just saw - 1D106, which was the report dated 12th of July, report of the CSB, and P989, which is the report of your inspectors, dated the 30th of May - in both of these documents, they nominate inspectors, or operatives. Or, rather, the operatives nominate Brano Vlaco as inspector of the administration for crime suppression. Does this refer to this particular Brano Vlaco, with a moustache, who was inspector for corporate crime at the town SUP of Sarajevo before the war?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly him, precisely him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this Brano Vlaco, after a certain time, probably having gotten acquainted with the situation in Vogosca, packed his bags and set off for Bijeljina. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. But I believe that for a short while he worked at the SDK of Vogosca municipality, while the clearance system was still functioning. He worked there for a short while and then he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But at any rate, he left the Vogosca SJB, worked for a while for the SDK, and after a short period, he went to Bijeljina; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that man now lives in Bijeljina and is a bank manager there; right? Brano Vlaco.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's the manager of the Raiffeisen Bank in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Raiffeisen Bank. The other Brano Vlaco, whom you also know, was a member of the special unit of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina before the war; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you saw him on 8 June 1992 at Kalovita Brda.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You didn't see him from 1 April through 8 June, or did you?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing him then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you saw him on 8 June - and you remember the 8th of June because of the large-scale Muslim offensive - he said to you that somebody -- he had an appointment with somebody -- rather, a job interview, to be employed by the MUP of the RS; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But after some 20 to 30 minutes, according to you, there was a phone call made to Kalovita Brda that the Muslims had attacked Vogosca, and he jumped in his car and set off for Vogosca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And, basically, you know that on that day he didn't go to that job interview; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He returned. And the minister didn't come on that day. Because I spent most of the day at Kalovita Brda. I didn't see him there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After the 8th of June, you never saw this second Brano Vlaco again, the one we have just talked about? I mean in 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw him after the war, but not before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you don't know what happened to him after the 8th of June, do you?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe that the Prosecutor told me -- or, rather, he asked me whether he became commander at Vogosca in late 1992. So he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'll show you document 1D339; 65 ter 1435. Mr. Planojevic, you told me that the Prosecutor asked you about Brano Vlaco and his appointment in November when he became commander, or something, at the Vogosca SJB. Did the OTP, during the proofing, show you this document, dated 21 July 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not one document was shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you can make it out. This is document of the Ministry of Justice. I believe you can read that. It is marked 01-131, Sarajevo, 21 July 1992. And it says: "Decision." I don't know whether can you read that.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read that, as well as the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Brano Vlaco from Vogosca shall be appointed warden of the detention department of the penal and correctional facility Butmir at Ilidza, located in Vogosca. And the last sentence: "This ruling shall enter into force on the day of its passing and shall apply from 14 July 1992." And on behalf of the Ministry of Justice, Mr. Avlijas signed the decision. I suppose you haven't seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this Brano Vlaco, in July, was appointed warden -- prison warden by the Ministry of Justice of the RS?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only see it now. I didn't know it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, we have about a quarter hour left, and I'll introduce another topic. You may remember that an hour, an hour and a half ago we discussed the role of the ministry as a body giving out instructions. And there were work instructions, suggestions, and we mentioned that the -- the controlling role of the ministry. So tell me whether the MUP of the RS ever issued any instruction known to you, as assistant minister, about discrimination of non-Serbs in the activities of the police?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen anything like that or heard of its existence. And if I had, I certainly would have reacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was an attitude, without a written order or official instructions, and was there an overall attitude of discrimination of non-Serbs in the MUP of the RS while you were there?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to the executive officials of the ministries, then my answer is: No, absolutely not, as far as I can tell from my contacts that I had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you about the contacts that you may have had with regard to the fact that you were assistant minister and, later, you worked in the National Security Service.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. There were no such documents or deeds or behaviour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It comes as no surprise, I would imagine, that there would be no written instructions from the top of the ministry to discriminate non-Serbs. So your next question to the witness, when he had confirmed that no such instructions were known to him, was whether he was aware of any attitude that would favour discrimination, and Mr. Planojevic answered that no such attitude existed in the executive level, as far as he was aware. So that begs the question whether the witness - you, Mr. Planojevic - were aware if any such attitude existed at lower levels of the MUP organisation. Can you help us out here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's difficult for me to answer that question. I didn't have that many contacts. Most of my contacts were indirect. If you consider the times, I had no time to contact anybody than -- other than my closest co-workers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a fact, isn't it ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact, isn't it, that while you were assistant minister of the interior of the RS all instructions from the ministry to the CSBs in the territory of the RS, and consequently to the local SJBs, insisted on, above all, obeying the law and act -- the police acting in accordance with laws and regulations; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And there were many such orders; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, considering all the circumstances, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's exactly what I want to ask you, about the reason of repeatedly issuing orders and stressing duties that clearly stem from the law. Isn't it true that due to the objective situation and the war, the Ministry of Interior, to make sure that it gets through to the lowest level - the SJBs - repeatedly sent out orders with basically the same contents?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- that's true. But you had to be flexible. When I say "flexible," I mean that you had to balance things. Whether it was justified to, say, sacrifice a village, or not insist on things, and I've already explained the conditions under which we worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand you fully. But that -- that's why one of your instructions said that all cases must be documented. But we'll get there yet. Apart from the inspectors who were sent out by Cedo Kljajic in late May 1992 to Vogosca and Ilijas, the inspectors of the MUP were also sent to other places in the RS whenever they were able to make it to some CSBs or SJBs; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'll show you some documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 1D00-0513.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you said some documents. It's two minutes before we rise for the evening. Is it possible to finish these, quote/unquote, documents within that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, definitely not. But one I can, if I may, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. [Interpretation] 1D0513.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'll remind you: Danilo Vukovic was a crime inspector of the MUP of the RS; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And he was in your administration; right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a document dated 24 June 1992, I believe, and it authorises Danilo Vukovic to engage in some activity in the territory of the Bijeljina CSB, the Bijeljina SJB, and, well, in the east of the RS; and he coordinates and directs the work of the crime investigation services there. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe the signature is that of Mr. Njegus, correct, or that of Cedo Kljajic?

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's Kljajic's. But it -- maybe it's Radomir's, after all; I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But, at any rate, you know that Danilo Vukovic, in June, had the authority to visit the CSB of Bijeljina and some CSBs in the east of the RS.

utterances.speaker: DOBRISLAV PLANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there's opposition, I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D391, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Planojevic. We will continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe it's proper time to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, may I ask a question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to know whether I will be free tomorrow, so I can plan my activities. Will we finish tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I believe I will be able to finish, I don't know, one session, maybe a bit longer than one session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'd inquired of the Court Officer as to how much time had you left, and I was calculating, and I -- from what he had said in terms of what you had left, I was thinking we might not finish this witness tomorrow, but I'm anxious -- I'm glad to learn that you are alive to this and that, to answer the witness's question, it seems as if we are headed in that direction. Mr. Krgovic, we had had an hour and a half for you. Is that still the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't think that we have any cross for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... so, Mr. Planojevic, to answer your question, it appears that we, more likely than not, would be completed your testimony tomorrow. Yes. I believe we are in Courtroom II tomorrow. Yes. So 9.00 tomorrow morning.
